newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House Democratic leader Gephardt tours Iowa.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House Democratic leader Gephardt tours Iowa.

text.p: House Democratic leader Richard Gephardt Saturday toured Iowa, the scene of an early victory in his fizzled 1988 presidential bid, but sidestepped questions about his intentions for 2000.
The minority leader was helping state Democrats raise money, meeting with the media and encouraging a local Democrat who is planning to run for the U.S. House of Representatives.

Gephardt's trip came one month after Vice President Al Gore toured the state to make clear he intended to campaign hard to win Iowa's caucuses in 2000. The caucuses backed Gephardt in 1988, but his campaign later ran out of money and he stopped seeking the Democratic presidential nomination.
Gephardt publicly evaded questions about current presidential aspirations, giving reporters the same answer he gave during a springtime visit to Iowa.

"I'm interested in one thing -- representing a half million people in Missouri ... and on trying to bring back the right values and the right policies to the House of Representatives by winning a majority in the House in 1998," he said.
One of Gephardt's events was staged on Peter Thurman's farm just outside of Marion. Thurman supported Gephardt's 1988 presidential bid and said he was leaning toward him over Gore.
Gephardt used a cornfield news conference to blast Republican-led efforts to scuttle federal tax breaks for corn-based ethanol fuel. Ethanol's tax advantages are set to expire in three years.
"Ethanol equals jobs, equals a strong economy in the Midwest," Gephardt said.
The Senate has endorsed extending the tax advantages to 2007. The budget agreement President Clinton intends to sign Tuesday does not contain anything about the issue.
